title: Which probe becomes the center?
hook: Two scored candidates compete to move a search.

knows: a search can get stuck in a local valley
larger signed scores can be compared
doesNotKnow: how scored perturbations select a new center
why this finite ES-style toy is not CMA-ES or a general optimality guarantee

misconception: An optimizer must receive derivatives to make progress.
objective: Trace a fixed-offset perturb/evaluate/select search move that consumes positions and scores without derivatives.

claims.text: The fixed-offset toy evaluates score −(x−3)^2. At center 0 its score is −9, probes −1/+1 score −16/−4, and the higher-score winner is 1. At center 1 probes 0/2 score −9/−1, selecting 2. The first control runs and retains both rounds; Reset preserves both retained rows.
claims.source: Independent derivation and source audit: company/reviews/evolution-strategies/2026-10-19-fact-all-ai-foundations.md; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.03864 (section 2, PDF p.2, lines 61–88); src/demos/ai/evolution-strategies/model.ts and Demo.tsx. Registered recall verified separately; shared footer coverage gap remains.

claims.text: The winner update uses positions and scores without derivatives. This fixed-offset ES-style toy is not CMA-ES or an optimality guarantee.

recall.question: Two probes return scores −8 and −2. Which does the higher-score rule select?
recall.why: The higher-score rule compares the supplied scores; it needs no derivative.
